target_customer: Spanish speaking consumers who want weight loss or muscle gain meal plans and calorie tracking, via a freemium app with premium subscriptions
problem: People want to improve their diet but cannot afford a nutritionist, and generic calorie counters do not adapt plans to their foods and progress.
business_model: Consumer freemium app with a premium subscription for meal plans, shopping lists and advanced tools
product_category: AI meal planner and calorie counter app

founders.name: Piero Linares
prior_employers: Grupo Breca (finance and business development, almost four years, started as intern)

founders.name: Ulises Olave
prior_employers: Telefonica (intern, analyst at Telefonica Empresas, product manager for financial institution products)
education: Specialization in software management and digital development

competitors.name: MyFitnessPal
competitors.what: Calorie counter with paid meal planner

competitors.name: Eat This Much
competitors.what: Generates weekly meal plans from calorie goals and preferences

competitors.name: Yazio
competitors.what: Calorie counting with meal planning and fasting support

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a verified regional food database and plan generation that adapts to progress; standard mobile engineering with data work in Spanish speaking markets.

defensibility.rationale: Localized food data and Spanish language focus help, but large trackers can add meal plans and the app category has low switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept their products and Fitia claims over 20 million users on its own site; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Fitness and nutrition app use was high in 2021 and the Spanish speaking market had few localized planners; the founders say the idea came from friends who could not afford a nutritionist.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, claims backed by nutrition team verified data

branding.brand_signature: Self reported 4.9 star rating and 20 million user claim
branding.community_and_virality: Featured in Apple App Store stories per search results; publishes many comparison articles on its own site.

brand_strength.rationale: Apple App Store editorial features and a large self reported user base suggest decent visibility, but no independent brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Fitia launched in July 2019 as a Peru pilot, joined YC in 2021 and says it now has over 20 million users, though that figure is self reported. A 2024 profile reports about 800,000 monthly active users, a team near 20 and a seed round from US investors without amounts. Growth looks product led and efficient, while funding disclosure is thin.
notes: The 125,000 USD YC figure is from the Infomercado article which says 7 percent; it is the standard YC deal reported there, recorded as other. The seed round amount and investors are not stated. Startup Peru 8G+ seed capital in 2022 is mentioned without amount. Competitor sources are undated 2026 comparison pages; the apps existed before 2021 but no dated 2021 source was found. User counts differ (800,000 monthly active in 2024 vs 20 million users claimed on site).
